text:
incident-bot: 🔔 PAGE: high-severity alert — GPU pool 'redwood-gpu-prod' at 100% capacity, queue growth > 6k requests, request latency spiking > 3s, autoscaler not adding nodes. Paging on-call: @alice.sre, @dan.oncall.

alice.sre: on it. seeing 0 available nodes in pool, pods Pending because HPA target metric not updating.

bob.mlinfra: logs from metrics-adapter: `error converting metrics from prometheus: timed out` — adapter restarted twice in last 10m.

carol.runtime: customer-facing APIs show 429s from the router and token-level spikes. Some hosted tenants on Dedicated see degraded throughput.

dan.oncall: quick check: HPA for gpu-deployment shows desired=0 current=0 because `custom/gpu_queue_length` metric is stale. Prom scrape time shows gap.

alice.sre: stack: prometheus -> prometheus-adapter -> kube-metrics-server? we use custom adapter for queue length. If adapter is failing, HPA won't scale.

metrics-bot: prom-scrape: failed targets 17/120, last error `context deadline exceeded`. Adapter logs: `500: internal conversion error`.

frank.sre-lead: @bob.mlinfra @carol.runtime coordinate immediate mitigations: 1) reduce ingress to hosted API (rate-limit), 2) shift critical tenants to reserve nodes, 3) attempt manual scale of GPU nodegroup. Which can we do fastest?

bob.mlinfra: manual scale possible via cloud autoscaling grp. Command I will run: `cloudctl nodegroup scale redwood-gpu-prod --count 6` — but that will take ~3-6m to join and warm. Meanwhile adapter restart attempt: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter` (doing now).

carol.runtime: applying rate limits on non-critical routes: `POST /v1/generate` for free-tier -> 40% throttle. Pushing config to edge now.

alice.sre: I'm going to switch HPA to fallback metric (cpu) temporarily for gpu-deployment to allow basic scaling. Patch: `kubectl patch hpa gpu-deployment -p '{"spec":{"metrics":[{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"type":"Utilization","averageUtilization":60}}}]}}'`

dan.oncall: on it. Patching HPA to CPU fallback. Note: pods need node GPU access; cpu-scaling might make more pods pending if no GPUs available. We'll do nodegroup scale concurrently.

bob.mlinfra: prometheus-adapter restarted; logs show initial errors but now `registration successful` and `metrics served: custom/gpu_queue_length`. HPA metrics now showing values again.

metrics-bot: adapter -> metric scrape latency reduced to 2.1s, metric `custom/gpu_queue_length` updated 00:00:16 ago.

carol.runtime: manual nodegroup scale accepted by cloud — 6 extra nodes requested, expected to be ready ~4m. Starting immediate placement for pending pods with tolerations.

erin.custsuccess: @carol.runtime can we get a quick statement for impacted customers? Some enterprise tenants reported sluggishness for a few minutes.

carol.runtime: sending temporary status: "We are experiencing higher than normal request latency for generation endpoints due to backend capacity strain. Mitigation in progress: autoscaler and metrics pipeline being restored, and additional GPU capacity being added. No data exposure."

frank.sre-lead: good. Keep customers updated every 15m. Priority: restore autoscale and reduce queue.

alice.sre: HPA now sees the custom metric and desired pods jumped from 0 -> 24. However scheduler is still pending because insufficient GPU nodes; new nodes are provisioning.

bob.mlinfra: while nodes spin up I'm enabling an emergency partial fallback: reroute high-cost jobs to smaller model variant (gpt-small) via runtime feature flag. This will reduce per-request GPU time. Pushing flag now.

carol.runtime: flag applied. Telemetry shows immediate drop in average GPU token-time by ~30%. Queue growth rate flattening.

metrics-bot: prom-scrape healthy. kube-metrics-server restart scheduled earlier completed — node-level metrics restored.

dan.oncall: nodes are joining: 3/6 ready so far. Pod placement is happening. We have ~10 new gpu-pods scheduled. Latency dropping slowly.

erin.custsuccess: received a reply from a customer: "Thanks for the quick update, some of our workflows timed out but we've queued them. Would appreciate ETA." I've responded that engineers expect steady recovery in next 10-15m.

alice.sre: confirm: queue length peaked at 6.2k, now down to 2.7k and dropping. 429s reduced by 80%.

frank.sre-lead: can we run a temporary autoscaler health check and record root cause? Two likely contributors: Prometheus scrape latency and adapter conversion errors causing HPA metric staleness. Need postmortem items: circuit breaker on adapter, faster fallback metric, and runbook updates.

bob.mlinfra: agree. I'm collecting logs: adapter stacktrace shows `panic: json: invalid use of ,string` when converting newer metric format from Prom. Looks like a metric label change after a recent Prom update. Will pin adapter to last known-good and submit PR to handle variant.

carol.runtime: runtime changes: added a rate-limit rule in edge and a fallback routing to dedicated spare pool. Also added a short TTL caching for repeated prefix sequences to help drain queue faster.

metrics-bot: recording outage window: start=2550006789, mitigation_entered=2550006822, partial_capacity_restore=2550006900, full_autoscale_restore=2550007075.

dan.oncall: full autoscale restored, HPA metrics stable, nodegroup at target +6. Current queue 400 and falling. Router 429s back to baseline.

erin.custsuccess: updating status page to "degraded service — mitigation complete, increased capacity added, autoscaling restored; ongoing follow-up."

alice.sre: closing the page after monitoring for 30m. Will kick off incident report template. Action items assigned: (1) bob.mlinfra - pin adapter + fix parsing, (2) frank.sre-lead - runbook update for fallback metric and adapter circuit breaker, (3) carol.runtime - add emergency traffic-shed knob to console, (4) dan.oncall - run GA test that simulates adapter downtime and ensures HPA fallback works.

frank.sre-lead: thumbs. Postmortem owners noted. Thanks all for quick response.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced to SEV2 — paging cleared.

alice.sre: leaving a short snippet to reproduce adapter error locally: `curl -sS http://prom:9090/api/v1/query?query=some_custom_metric | jq .data.result` then feed to adapter conversion. The label set with `raw_value` as string broke the converter.

bob.mlinfra: raising hotfix PR now and will schedule a canary release to infra tomorrow.

carol.runtime: I'll run a retrospective tomorrow with SRE and ML infra to go over telemetry and customer communications.

dan.oncall: handing off to @frank.sre-lead for post-incident tracking. I'm done with active mitigation.

frank.sre-lead: acknowledged. Leaving a note to update SLA register and check whether enterprise customers need credits.

erin.custsuccess: will follow up with affected accounts directly. Thanks everyone.

alice.sre: incident closed (monitor for 1h).
